# Budget Policy

**Every run is metered. The platform must deliver strong output _under budget_ — even leaning on Haiku — with no repeated work.** This doc is the single source of truth for what the budgets are, who can change them, and what happens when one is hit. It is **owned and enforced by `@supervisor`**, which tallies usage through the **`budget-check`** skill.

> If `budget-check` says STOP, the run STOPS. No agent overrides the ceiling.

---

## 1. The Three Enforced Budgets

| Budget | Default | What it counts | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_iterations` | **5** | Worker→`@critic`→fix loops per stage (an "iteration" = one produce-then-gate cycle). | `@supervisor` + `budget-check` |
| `cost_cap_usd` | **2.00** | Total USD spend across all model tiers for the whole run. | `@supervisor` + `budget-check` |
| `tool_budget` | **60 tool calls** _(POC value — **confirm with owner**)_ | Every tool invocation across every agent in the run (Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Grep/Glob/WebFetch + skill calls). | `@supervisor` + `budget-check` |

`@supervisor` allocates a slice of each budget to each planned stage up front, then calls `budget-check` between stages to reconcile actual against plan. Worker agents do not self-meter — they consume; `@supervisor` accounts.

> **POC note:** `tool_budget = 60` is a starting ceiling for this POC and must be **confirmed with the repo owner** before it is treated as final. Tune from real run telemetry, not guesswork.

---

## 2. Resolution Order (who sets the ceiling)

Budgets resolve from project config down to the individual agent. **The ceiling only ever goes _down_, never up.**

1. **`.eq-sparks.yml` (project) sets the CEILING.** This is the hard maximum for the run. If unset, the defaults in §1 apply.
2. **An agent MAY declare LOWER caps in its frontmatter** (e.g. a Haiku scanner that should never need more than 8 tool calls). A lower self-declared cap is honoured.
3. **An agent may NEVER declare a cap HIGHER than the project ceiling.** A higher value is clamped to the ceiling and the attempt is logged by `@supervisor`. It is not an error — it is silently capped and recorded for review.

```
project .eq-sparks.yml ceiling  >=  agent-declared cap  >=  actual spend
        (hard max)                   (may be lower)          (metered)
```

This lets the cheap-by-default model ladder (see **model-routing-policy**) keep tight per-agent caps while the project still owns the absolute spend.

---

## 3. On Exhaustion (any of the three budgets hit)

When `budget-check` reports a budget is exhausted, `@supervisor` runs this sequence — **in order, no skipping**:

1. **Emit telemetry.** Record which budget tripped, the stage, the iteration count, USD spend, tool-call count, and the responsible agent(s). This feeds future ceiling tuning.
2. **Run `self-evaluate`** on the best work produced so far. Mandatory — no handoff without it.
3. **Branch on the self-eval result:**
   - **PASS →** submit the work as **`[partial-budget]`**. The deliverable is real but explicitly flagged as truncated by budget so the human reviewer knows scope was cut, not completed.
   - **FAIL →** halt with **`BLOCKED:cost-cap`**. No partial submission. The run is parked for human go/no-go.

```
budget hit
   └─ emit telemetry
        └─ self-evaluate
             ├─ PASS  → submit  [partial-budget]
             └─ FAIL  → halt    BLOCKED:cost-cap
```

Both terminal states are surfaced through `console-render` in the run Summary so the outcome is never hidden.

---

## 4. Anti-Patterns (hard NO)

- **Never silently retry after a budget hit.** A retry that consumes more budget without `@supervisor` re-authorising it is a violation. The exhaustion sequence in §3 is the only legal next move.
- **Never silently switch to a smaller model to save tokens.** Downshifting a tier is a **`@supervisor` decision**, made and logged explicitly — not an unannounced cost-saving move by a worker. (Note: escalation _up_ a rung on low confidence is governed by **model-routing-policy**; the same "logged, never silent" rule applies in both directions.)
- **Never raise your own cap above the project ceiling** (see §2.3). Caps clamp down, never up.
- **Never spend without metering.** Work that bypasses `budget-check` accounting is not permitted.

---

## 5. How Tier Escalation Consumes Budget

Budget and the model ladder are coupled. See **model-routing-policy** for the full ladder, but for budgeting:

- Agents run at their **default tier** (HAIKU mechanical / SONNET codegen+specialists / OPUS judgment). Haiku-first keeps `cost_cap_usd` low by default.
- An agent escalates **one rung only** on low self-eval confidence (<0.7) or two `@critic` FAILs. **Every escalation is logged and charged against `cost_cap_usd`** — a Sonnet→Opus jump is materially more expensive and `@supervisor` accounts for it.
- Escalation also tends to add iterations; those count against `max_iterations`. An agent that has burned its iteration budget cannot escalate its way around the gate — it hits §3 instead.
- **Never auto-downgrade.** Saving budget by dropping a rung is a `@supervisor` decision per §4.

Caching is the other half of staying under budget: fetch/scan agents reuse `cache-lookup` results and build agents run `dna-precheck` first to avoid generating what already exists (see **cache-policy** and **dedup-policy**). Work avoided is budget saved.

---

## 6. Enforcement Summary

- **Owner / enforcer:** `@supervisor`.
- **Instrument:** the **`budget-check`** skill, called between stages and on any suspected overrun.
- **Reporting:** telemetry on every budget event; final tallies and any `[partial-budget]` / `BLOCKED:cost-cap` outcome rendered via `console-render`.
- **Authority:** `@supervisor` is the only role that may re-authorise spend, change tier, or call go/no-go on a budget-blocked run. Everything else honours the ceiling.
